title: Ravioles du Dauphiné
cScaleSummary: Estimated approximately 95–110 mg dietary cholesterol per appetizer serving (C3), conservatively counting the entire dough batch: one large egg contributes about 186 mg per batch, 60 g butter about 129 mg, 40 g Comté about 40–45 mg, and 80 g fromage blanc a variable amount depending on fat content. Divide the batch by four. Discarded dough lowers actual intake. This also contains substantial saturated fat.
ldlActiveSummary: Not LDL Active. This special-occasion recipe retains butter and cheese to reproduce the dish's defining flavors and uses refined-flour egg pasta. The mushroom jus supplies flavor but does not make the dish fiber-forward.
intro: Inspired by Chef Cassidy Visconti’s cheese course at the Bonita Bay Club chef dinner on October 27, 2026, Dave’s favorite dish of the evening. This is a home reconstruction, not the chef’s recipe, and has not yet been kitchen-tested. Paper-thin pasta encloses small pockets of fromage blanc and Comté in connected two-by-three sheets, finished with mushroom jus emulsified with brown butter and fresh chervil. Makes approximately 16 sheets, each about 4 by 2 inches; serve four sheets per appetizer portion. The defining texture is delicate pasta with low cheese cushions. Butter and cheese are retained deliberately for this special-occasion entry.

miseEnPlace: Drain {{ingredient:fromage-blanc}} in a fine sieve in the refrigerator until thick and no longer weeping; weigh after draining.
Finely grate {{ingredient:comte}}, slice {{ingredient:cremini}} and {{ingredient:shallot}}, and pick {{ingredient:chervil}}.
Stage a pasta machine, piping bag, pastry wheel, ruler, fine sieve, light-colored saucepan, wide cooking pan, and wide slotted spatula. Measure the remaining ingredients.

stepGroups.title: Make the pasta dough
items: Mix {{quantity:flour}} flour with {{quantity:egg}} egg. Knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and firm. If dry crumbs will not incorporate, wet your fingertips with a little of {{ingredient:assembly-water}} and continue kneading; do not add the entire measured amount.
Wrap tightly and rest at room temperature for 45–60 minutes. Start the jus during the rest.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the filling
items: Blend {{quantity:fromage-blanc}} drained fromage blanc, {{quantity:comte}} Comté, and {{quantity:pepper}} pepper into a smooth, thick paste using a small processor or by pressing and mixing thoroughly. The paste should hold a small mound without leaking.
Transfer to a piping bag and refrigerate while preparing the jus. The cheese supplies the filling's salt.

stepGroups.title: Build and strain the mushroom jus
items: Soak {{quantity:porcini}} porcini in {{quantity:soaking-water}} hot water for 20 minutes. Lift out the mushrooms and strain the soaking liquid through a damp coffee filter or paper towel-lined sieve to remove grit.

Heat {{quantity:oil}} oil in a wide saucepan over medium-high heat. Add {{quantity:cremini}} cremini and cook, stirring occasionally, until their liquid evaporates and they brown, about 10–15 minutes. Add {{quantity:shallot}} shallot and cook 2–3 minutes.
Add {{quantity:wine}} wine and scrape up the browned bits. Reduce until almost dry. Add {{quantity:stock}} stock, the soaked porcini, and filtered soaking liquid. Simmer gently for 25–30 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing lightly. Discard the solids from this sauce. Reduce the strained liquid to 120 ml per base batch, about 1/2 cup. It should taste distinctly mushroomy. Set aside.

stepGroups.title: Brown the butter
items: Melt {{quantity:butter}} butter in a small light-colored saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir and scrape the bottom as it foams. When the milk solids are golden brown and smell nutty, immediately transfer all the butter and browned bits to a heatproof bowl.
Let cool until warm. Brown butter must not be sizzling hot when it is added to the jus.

stepGroups.title: Roll and assemble connected sheets
items: Divide the rested dough in half and keep one half wrapped. Roll the other through progressively thinner machine settings, using {{ingredient:bench-flour}} sparingly. Aim for about 0.4–0.5 mm thick, translucent but strong enough to handle. Machine settings vary; do not force dough through a setting that tears it.

Work in short sections so the surface stays supple. On the bottom layer, mark rectangles about 4 by 2 inches. Pipe six small dots of filling into each rectangle in two rows of three, about a scant 1/4 teaspoon per pocket. Divide the filling across approximately 16 sheets, keeping the pockets low.

Brush excess flour from sealing areas. Moisten the sealing lines very lightly with {{ingredient:assembly-water}} only if the dough has become dry. Lay a second thin sheet over the filling. Press out air around each mound, then seal the perimeter and the grid between pockets with your fingertips or a blunt chopstick. Do not cut through the internal seams.

Trim only the outside edge of each rectangle, leaving six connected pockets. Gently reroll clean scraps once after resting them wrapped for 15 minutes. Expect some unused scraps; prioritize thinness over using every scrap.
Place sheets separately on a lightly floured parchment-lined tray without stacking. Cover with a clean towel while finishing the batch. Cook promptly.

stepGroups.title: Cook the ravioles
items: Bring {{quantity:cooking-water}} water and {{quantity:salt}} salt to a gentle simmer in a wide pan. Warm four shallow serving bowls. Set the mushroom jus over low heat.

Cook one test sheet first. Start checking after 60 seconds; approximately 1–2 minutes may suffice, but thickness determines the time. The sealed pasta edges should be tender and the center hot. Adjust the remaining cooking time to the test sheet.

Cook the remaining sheets in small batches without crowding or vigorous boiling. Reserve {{quantity:reserved-water}} cooking water for the sauce. Lift sheets with a wide slotted spatula, drain briefly, and arrange directly in warm bowls. Work quickly; do not hold cooked sheets piled together.

stepGroups.title: Emulsify the sauce and serve
items: Take the warm mushroom jus off the heat. Gradually whisk in the warm brown butter and its browned milk solids. For a more uniform emulsion, use an immersion blender in a narrow heatproof vessel, keeping the blade submerged.

Whisk in {{quantity:lemon}} lemon juice. Add reserved pasta water a teaspoon at a time only as needed for a glossy, lightly coating consistency. If the sauce separates, blend it again with a small splash of warm water. Keep warm gently and do not boil.
Spoon the sauce over and around the sheets, dividing it evenly between portions. Finish with {{quantity:chervil}} chervil and serve immediately.
